name: Colored lenses / blue light glasses
lead: Colored lenses and blue-light glasses are spectacles with tinted or filtered lenses marketed to reduce eye strain from screens and, in some looksmaxxing circles, to reduce puffiness around the eyes. By the late 2010s such glasses became popular, with claims ranging from dry eyes and eye strain to sleep disruption and macular degeneration.[1]

Wikipedia reports that the American Academy of Ophthalmology does not recommend special eyewear for computer use and that the UK College of Optometrists says evidence does not support blue-blocking lenses for the general population.[1] No studies were found on tinted lenses reducing eye puffiness.
infobox: Less eye strain, better sleep, less puffiness

paras: Some products filter blue light from screens, and some are also claimed to block ultraviolet light; Wikipedia states that computer monitors emit no measurable UV.[1] Yellow-tinted computer glasses are said to offer slight colour correction and to reduce strain from reduced blinking, though the article supports this with commercial sources rather than controlled studies.[1]

The article says long continuous screen use, not blue light, is the likely cause of digital eye strain, and that several studies indicate computer blue light does not cause eye diseases such as macular degeneration. The AAO suggests prescription glasses measured for screen distance where needed, and reducing evening screen time to help sleep.[1]
Tinted lenses are claimed in appearance communities to reduce eye strain or puffiness. No community sources were available to quote.
No studies found on appearance outcomes such as eye puffiness. Studies of blue-blocking lenses for eye strain are discussed in the broader literature, not tested here.

lore.intro: Tinted lenses are mentioned as a minor appearance accessory.

claims.claim: Blue-light glasses reduce eye strain and eye puffiness
claims.believers: Proponents say less screen strain means less eye fatigue and a fresher look.
claims.experts: The AAO does not recommend special eyewear for computer use, and the College of Optometrists says evidence does not support blue-blocking lenses in the general population.[1] No studies tested effects on puffiness.

card.summary: Tinted blue-light lenses sold for eye strain and fresher-looking eyes; eye-care bodies cited by Wikipedia do not recommend them.
card.note: No studies on eye puffiness; eye-care bodies do not recommend them for general use.

quick.overview:
These are tinted or blue-filtering lenses marketed for screen eye strain and sometimes for less eye puffiness.

The AAO and UK College of Optometrists, as reported by Wikipedia, do not recommend them for general use, and no studies were found on puffiness.
quick.mechanism: Coatings or tints absorb part of the blue end of the light spectrum; yellow tints may slightly adjust colour.
quick.risks: Low physical risk. Colour distortion can occur with strongly tinted lenses, and benefits are unproven.
